answer_text: The printing press, developed by Johannes Gutenberg in the mid-15th century, revolutionized how written material could be produced by introducing movable metal type that could be rearranged and reused to print many copies of a page far faster than any scribe copying by hand ever could. Before the printing press, books had to be laboriously copied out by hand, one at a time, usually by monks or professional scribes, which made books extremely expensive, time-consuming to produce, and available only to a small, wealthy, or religious elite.
